assertions.description: overflow: scroll clip parses (note: parsing alone predates this feature — the computed-value assertions below are the real test).
The clip half is no longer legacy-converted: an element declared overflow: scroll clip computes overflow-y to clip (legacy engines compute hidden).
assertions.test: (()=>{ const el = document.createElement('div'); el.style.cssText = 'overflow: scroll clip; width: 40px; height: 40px;'; document.body.appendChild(el); const v = getComputedStyle(el).overflowY; el.remove(); return v === 'clip'; })()

assertions.description: An axis set to clip cannot be moved from 0 by script (scrollTop assignment) even when content overflows — unlike hidden, which remains script-scrollable.
assertions.test: (()=>{ const el = document.createElement('div'); el.style.cssText = 'overflow: scroll clip; width: 60px; height: 40px;'; const inner = document.createElement('div'); inner.style.cssText = 'width: 200px; height: 200px;'; el.appendChild(inner); document.body.appendChild(el); el.scrollTop = 50; const stuck = el.scrollTop === 0; el.remove(); return stuck && (()=>{ const h = document.createElement('div'); h.style.cssText = 'overflow: scroll hidden; width: 60px; height: 40px;'; const hi = document.createElement('div'); hi.style.cssText = 'width: 200px; height: 200px;'; h.appendChild(hi); document.body.appendChild(h); h.scrollTop = 50; const moved = h.scrollTop > 0; h.remove(); return moved; })(); })()

assertions.description: The scroll half keeps working: the horizontal axis of an overflow: scroll clip element remains script-scrollable when content overflows horizontally.
assertions.test: (()=>{ const el = document.createElement('div'); el.style.cssText = 'overflow: scroll clip; width: 60px; height: 40px;'; const inner = document.createElement('div'); inner.style.cssText = 'width: 300px; height: 20px;'; el.appendChild(inner); document.body.appendChild(el); el.scrollLeft = 50; const moved = el.scrollLeft > 0; el.remove(); return moved; })()

assertions.description: scroll clip and scroll hidden serialize as distinct computed values — the legacy aliasing is gone in both directions.
assertions.test: (()=>{ const mk = (v) => { const el = document.createElement('div'); el.style.cssText = 'overflow: ' + v + '; width: 40px; height: 40px;'; document.body.appendChild(el); const c = getComputedStyle(el).overflow; el.remove(); return c; }; return mk('scroll clip') !== mk('scroll hidden'); })()

assertions.description: position: sticky inside an overflow: scroll clip wrapper is constrained per axis: sticky top answers to the nearest ancestor that scrolls vertically (e.g. the page), not the wrapper.
assertions.test: Requires visual/scroll interaction: on the sticky-per-axis-stage demo, scroll the page and verify the header row tracks the viewport rather than being trapped by the wrapper, while row labels still stick against the wrapper's horizontal pan.
